evidence.activity: In-house technology and innovation teams of programmers and designers who build the bank's digital customer experience
evidence.quote: Our in-house technology division and innovation teams, together employing approximately 65 programmers and designers, support these business lines and their customer experience objectives.

creativity.criterion: level 1: in-house designers used only as a routine business input

evidence.activity: Employee volunteering in the communities the bank serves, tracked company-wide by hours
evidence.quote: We track our community services hours, which totaled over 29,000 in 2025, or approximately 10 hours per employee.
evidence.indicators: over 29,000 community services hours in 2025; approximately 10 hours per employee

community.criterion: level 3: measured, company-wide volunteering covering financial education and economic development, with hour totals as indicators

evidence.activity: Employee learning and development, including in-house learning and support for conferences, degrees, licenses and certifications
evidence.quote: In particular, we not only provide a number of in-house learning opportunities but also facilitate the educational and professional development of our employees through support to attend conferences and obtain degrees, licenses and certifications.

community.criterion: level 2: employee development of any size

evidence.activity: Ordinary lending and treasury services to small and other business customers
evidence.quote: Our long-tenured commercial lending teams originate loans to finance a wide range of our customers’ needs, including commercial, small business and government segments, while striving to maintain conservative underwriting standards.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Our Business Lines > Commercial Banking
evidence.indicators: approximately 69,000 small, middle-market and commercial business entities

entrepreneurship.criterion: level 1: small-business customers with no specific enabling service

creativity.reason: Level 1: the only creative activity is in-house designers used as a routine input to the bank's technology, and no creative product or arts activity is described.

community.reason: Level 3: measured community volunteering of over 29,000 hours in 2025 (about 10 hours per employee), including financial education, is community investment with substantial reach shown by indicators, alongside employee development.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 1: based only on general language ('cultivating an inclusive, safe and healthy workplace', 'serve a diverse customer base'), with no specific inclusion, accessibility or multilingual activity described.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 1: the bank serves small-business customers through ordinary lending, deposits and treasury/merchant services, but describes no specific program aimed at barriers to starting or growing a business.

ai.notes: Volunteering appears twice in Item 1 (culture 'Community Aligned' bullet and Employees section, which lists financial education, economic development, human and health services and community reinvestment, plus a new program to track and reward hours); it is counted once as E2. Community 3 rests on volunteer-hour figures only, with no dollars or named program, so it is near the 2/3 boundary. Not counted: 'community bank' wording; sponsorships of community events, which are part of the deposit-marketing strategy; the CRA 'satisfactory' rating, which is regulatory; Wealth Management help with foundations' grant applications and endowments, which is a fee-based commercial service; unquantified 'community outreach' expenses in Item 7 Corporate/Other; SBA securities held as investments; 'state-of-the-art' and 'innovative' trap language. The Bank is a plaintiff in the lawsuit challenging the CFPB rule requiring small-business lending data collection, including data on women- and minority-owned businesses. This is recorded for context only and is not scored. Planned branch expansion and a planned private banking expansion are not relevant to any theme.
